correctness.rationale: Berger tilting by t^n fixes mean m and variance v=m(s-m), and w_{n+h}²=E X^{h+1}/E X^h. The candidate two-atom laws {c,b} and {a,d} have matching first two moments. For h>=2 the Hermite division of t^{h+1}-lambda t^h by (t-c)^2(t-b) or (t-a)(t-d)^2 has nonnegative polynomial quotient because complete homogeneous coefficients dominate the maximal node; the divisor sign proves both ratio inequalities and equality support. For h=1 the ratio is already fixed. Strict support positivity permits inverse tilt t^-n, proving attainability for every n; mixing laws gives every intermediate ratio. Checked an independent exact three-atom instance across h=1..6. Numeric/LP grids are not universal proofs.
